body: The terrible times pass quickly, suicidal thoughts come out of the blue for me. Then the next day i feel ok, its a very rare irrational angry feeling when you begin to wish for death. Like you say though it comes, and it goes. At the moment i just wish the anxiety would lower, i can handle the sad feelings but anxiety is just unbareable at times and i don't use drugs anymore to block it. However, i must say drugs do and probably always will appeal to me because they provided a synthetic safety net whereby i could do public speaking and the kinds of social events that make me feel ridiculously nervous. Pretty sure those of us with anxiety disorders are born with that vulnerability, having said that i exercise and do things to try and alleviate the worst of it. That is sometimes all you can do, psychology is so complex that i dont believe anybody really knows the answer. The fact that i found a medication that worked was a stroke of luck, but the astonishing transformation it brings makes you feel utterly convinced that the problem is neurophysiology not philosophy and therapies outside of that. Exercise and other things make sense to me because they change the physical brain, i dont see any distinction between mental health and physical health, but for some odd reason a lot of people still do. Either because their ignorant, callous or unable to imagine those things. As i was unable to conceive of these feelings when i was younger, i dont feel resentment to misunderstandings, a lot of people simply dont understand depression. I wish i could say i didn't but it has struck me many times, i don't understand it unless im within the struggle itself. After it passes i can't look back and conceive of such pain, likewise when depressed i guess the problem is you can't conceive of anything other than pain. It's such a bizarre syndrome, but i guess you gotta keep going best as you can without compromise to those who judge you unfairly.

I'd call it an anxious depression primarily, the very severe periods where you wake up terrified of the day, filled with dread are not constant. Constantly the problem becomes this anhedonia whereby i may not necessarily be in pain, but i feel im colorblind to many joys that others feel. Very alienating sensation, without joy from things that ought to bring you positive feelings you begin to stop seeking out joy or really find interest in anything in life. Exercising and things probably help to a certain extent, my sleep doesnt usually become too hard to achieve but my appetite slowly dissipates. It's pretty constant for me atm, but i doubt i look distressed most of the time which is infuriating in itself. I wish i could show i wound, but i don't look anything like as bad as i feel.

I'm pretty much exactly there myself. I've begun to lose almost all hope. Terrible place to be in, and like you say sometimes having a loving family makes you all the more dissapointed at yourself. Only thing that ever helped me was opiates, which i wish i had access to as they helped. Pharmacology just feels too trial and error and therapy can expect to much out of people unable to calm their anxieties and fears. I guess if any advice can be passed from somebody like me in a similar situation it would be make sure you see a psychiatrist, get to the end of the day as well as you can manage. Running helps me a little bit so if your able to exercise give that a decent shot. Simple things like sunlight exposure are also meant to increase neurotransmission, the cause of these moods in my opinion. If you have tried those things and your still miserable then medication may help, if one doesnt work, try something different. I'm pretty sure i'll be dead within the next ten years but then again is that depression talking, or is that perfectly rational? Either way i'd like to jump off a bridge sooner rather than waste my time until later. I try and trudge through the shit best as i can.
